lina chen: Heads-up — during the int8 canary for raptor-v2 we saw ~0.7% of structured toolcalls return extra tokens after the JSON block. Breaking some call handlers.

mike: Can you paste a minimal example of the output?

lina chen: Sure — this is from a failing request (trimmed):

```
{"action":"create_ticket","args":{"priority":"p2","summary":"db lag"}}
\nAlso: check the DB replica streams — lag spikes around 03:12.
```

mike: Ugh — so the model appends a natural-language note after finishing the JSON. That will fail strict JSON parse. Is this only on int8?

lina chen: It’s correlated with the int8 build. On fp16 the same prompt returns a clean single-object JSON. On int8 we get three variants: clean JSON, JSON+comment, or two concatenated JSON objects (no newline).

arya: @lina chen can you share the request config? streaming vs non-streaming? prefix kv cache?

lina chen: Non-streaming in the canary; kv prefix enabled (we suspect truncation/stop-token heuristics interacting with quantized logits). prompt attached: short system + function schema.

infra-bot: Canary run 2026-03-18T03:12:12Z — raptor-v2-int8 — 512 samples processed — 3 failed parse events (0.59%) — Failing pattern: trailing NL + free text.

mike: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) post-process by extracting first JSON object (robust but loses second-object cases). 2) switch canary to NDJSON/stream sentinel so each object is on its own line and we parse per-line. Thoughts?

arya: Also consider inserting a clarifying instruction into the prompt: "Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else. If you must comment, put it in the 'debug' field as a string." That often reduces free-text tails. But for quantized onboards we should have a parse-rescue layer.

lina chen: I prototyped a lightweight repair step: try json.loads; on failure run regex to extract first balanced {...} block; if still failing, try NDJSON split by closing brace pattern. It rescued ~80% of current fails in local sim.

mike: Can we include a quick example of the regex approach?

lina chen: Sure:

```
# naive rescue: extract first {...} with balanced braces
m = re.search(r"\{(?:[^{}]|(?R))*\}", text, flags=re.S)
if m:
  payload = m.group(0)
  obj = json.loads(payload)
```

mike: Nice. Two operational TODOs: 1) add that rescue as a configurable postprocess step for the canary pipeline (opt-in), 2) run an amended canary with an extra prompt guard to see if rate of trailing-text drops.

arya: One more thought — detect concatenated JSON objects by scanning for '}{' or '}\n{' at the top-level and treat as NDJSON. That catches the double-object case without heavy heuristics.

lina chen: Agreed. Also opened a small eval to compare fp16 vs int8 for these parsing failure modes across 5k prompts. Initial numbers: fp16: 0.02% failures, int8: 0.65%.

infra-bot: Eval job 2699-03 queued — dataset=toolcall-canary-5k — expected runtime 18m.

mike: If the rescue step becomes standard, add a metric to the console: "structured_parse_rescue_rate" so we can track how often we repair outputs vs strict acceptance.

lina chen: Will do. For the longer-term fix we should test: (A) tune stop token/temperature behavior in quantized compile, (B) retrain small safety prompt instructing single-object output, (C) consider adding an explicit JSON sentinel like `===JSON_END===` after the object (model should emit it reliably).

arya: I pushed a tiny canary patch: json_rescue=true, ndjson_fallback=true, prompt_guard='single_object_only'. Running now. Will report back with failure delta.

canary-bot: Patch applied to canary-raptor-int8 at 2699-03-18T03:45Z — monitoring enabled.

lina chen: Great — if rescue rate is >0.5% we'll back off int8 rollout and investigate quant kernel differences.

mike: Thanks all. Capture action items: (1) Lina: add rescue lib + unit tests. (2) Arya: run 5k comparison and post result. (3) Infra: add console metric. (4) Eng-ML: consider sentinel option for canary prompt.

lina chen: Copy. Will update thread when we have numbers. :thumbsup:
